skill.name: accessibility-wcag
skill.description: Guide frontend accessibility work against WCAG 2.2 standards, including semantic HTML, alt text, keyboard access, focus handling, ARIA, labels, and contrast checks.
skill.summary: Guides WCAG 2.2 accessibility checks for frontend code and UI reviews.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: Static analyzer hits were false positives caused by Markdown code fences, CSS examples, keyboard-event text, and reference links in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, credential access, obfuscation, data exfiltration, or executable malware intent was found. The only residual concern is broad Bash permission for a skill that is mostly documentation and review guidance.

remediation.issue: Broad Bash permission for a documentation-centered skill
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools unless automated accessibility checks are required. If Bash remains, require explicit user confirmation before running install, npm, or Lighthouse commands.

remediation.issue: Package installation examples can modify a user environment
remediation.suggestion: Label npm install and Lighthouse CI commands as optional setup steps that should run only in a project owner-approved environment.

content.value_statement: Accessibility defects make products difficult to use and increase compliance risk. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through WCAG 2.2 checks for UI work.
actual_capabilities: Reviews UI patterns against WCAG 2.2 principles and checkpoints.
Guides semantic HTML choices for buttons, headings, forms, dialogs, and links.
Checks image alt text, form labels, ARIA attributes, and skip links.
Highlights keyboard access, focus visibility, focus obstruction, and target size issues.
Applies WCAG AA contrast thresholds for text, UI components, and graphics.
Suggests automated and manual accessibility test steps with axe, jsx-a11y, and Lighthouse CI.
limitations: It does not guarantee legal compliance for every jurisdiction or product type.
It cannot replace testing with disabled users and assistive technology users.
Automated tools may miss issues in content meaning, task flow, or screen reader experience.
Command examples should run only after user approval in the target project.

use_cases.title: Review a React Component
use_cases.description: Check a new component for labels, semantic elements, keyboard behavior, focus states, and ARIA usage before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Accessibility Audit
use_cases.description: Create a WCAG 2.2 review checklist with manual and automated test steps for a feature release.

use_cases.title: Improve Design Handoff Quality
use_cases.description: Translate accessibility requirements into concrete UI acceptance criteria for touch targets, contrast, focus, and alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Accessibility
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for WCAG 2.2 basics. Focus on semantic HTML, alt text, labels, keyboard access, and color contrast.

prompt_templates.title: Find Keyboard Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interaction for keyboard accessibility. Check tab order, focus visibility, Enter and Space behavior, escape behavior, and alternatives to dragging.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Release Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Team checklist before shipping a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a WCAG 2.2 AA checklist for this feature. Include automated tests, manual screen reader checks, contrast checks, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for WCAG 2.2 AA
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced remediation planning for existing UI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI code and propose a WCAG 2.2 AA remediation plan. Prioritize blockers, explain user impact, and suggest implementation steps.

output_examples.input: A custom clickable card uses a div, mouse click handling, and no focus style.
output_examples.output: The review flags missing semantic button behavior, missing keyboard activation, and hidden focus. It recommends a native button or complete role, tab, key, and focus support.

output_examples.input: A form uses placeholder text instead of labels for email and password fields.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing programmatic labels and explains the screen reader impact. It recommends visible labels linked to each input.

output_examples.input: A dashboard uses light gray text, icon-only controls, and drag-only sorting.
output_examples.output: The review reports contrast, name, and dragging alternative issues. It suggests stronger colors, accessible names, and move up or down buttons.

best_practices: Start with native HTML controls before adding ARIA roles or custom interaction code.
Test every critical workflow with only the keyboard before relying on automation results.
Document each accessibility fix with the user impact and the WCAG criterion it addresses.
anti_patterns: Replacing buttons and links with clickable div elements without keyboard support.
Using color alone to communicate errors, state, status, or required actions.
Adding ARIA attributes to hide structural problems instead of fixing semantic markup.

faq.question: Which WCAG version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets WCAG 2.2 and emphasizes AA requirements for common frontend work.

faq.question: Can it run automated accessibility tests?
faq.answer: It can suggest tools and commands, but any command should run only after user approval.

faq.question: Does it replace a full accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It supports code review and checklist creation, but full audits need manual testing and assistive technology review.

faq.question: Does it cover ARIA?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides dialog roles, live regions, busy states, labels, and when native HTML is better than ARIA.

faq.question: Can designers use it?
faq.answer: Yes. Designers can use it to create acceptance criteria for contrast, target size, focus, labels, and alternatives.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill provides review prompts and remediation guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
